content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all four figure briefs, tracing each claim limitation, numbered part, and figure statement back to the disclosure and the single USER passage in the conversation.

input.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight completed. I built a line-by-line ledger of all 16 claims (1-10 apparatus, 11-16 method), all 25 reference numerals (100, 102, 104, 106, 108, 110, 112, 114, 116, 118, 120, 122, 124, 126, 128, 130, 140, 202-216), every structural, relational, operational and result statement in the Field, Summary, Brief Description of Drawings, Detailed Description and Abstract, and all four figure briefs (FIG. 1 installation schematic, FIG. 2 connector channel, FIG. 3 controller block diagram, FIG. 4 flow diagram), and traced each item to an affirmative passage in input/disclosure.md or the single USER passage in input/conversation.md. The substantive core traces cleanly: the branch conductor and branch-limit-below-sum-of-ratings premise; per-channel contactor, connector current sensor, control-pilot interface and local connector identifier; the branch current sensor upstream of the contactors as an independent safety input; the isolated local bus to the connector interfaces and contactors; the stored charging authorization, requested current, minimum sustaining current and energy-deficit value; the per-interval subtraction of measured non-charging branch load and configurable safety reserve to obtain available charging current; minimum-sustaining-first assignment followed by energy-deficit distribution; pilot transmission of assigned limits and connector-sensor verification; reduced pilot command, verification interval and one-at-a-time ordered shedding in a stored shedding order until branch current is below the limit (claims 2/12's re-measure-and-stop is the direct entailment of "until"); the three reclosure conditions including the randomized recovery delay; welded-contactor recording above a leakage threshold with inhibition of the other contactors and operation of the local fault indicator; network interface, nonvolatile memory, signed local authorization token with expiry, last accepted branch limit, outage continuation, refusal of newly connected sessions, tamper-evident meter sequence and upload on return; and the service-input mapping by one low-energy pilot transition at a time with storage only on sensor agreement. Title, "Not applicable" cross-reference and "Not applicable" government-support statement match input/brief.md (no priority claim, no federally sponsored research); no means-plus-function language, both statutory classes present, no drafting notes, placeholders, open questions or unresolved alternatives remain, antecedent bases check out, the numeral ledger matches every numeral used in the text and briefs, FIG. 4's seven rectangles plus one diamond match the eight numbered steps 202-216, and the loop, branch and terminator paths match the described flow. There are no section lines or section views to cross-check. Four defects remain. One is substantive: the drafting verbalizes a connector-current sensing path that is affirmatively separate from and not joined to the isolated local bus, a topology the inventor never states (the disclosure says only that the controller "communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus" and is silent on how sensor readings reach it), so the exclusivity language must go while the inherently disclosed coupling may remain as a plain line. Three are internal-consistency defects: FIG-2's sensing line is told to end "at the upper boundary of the drawing area" although the same brief requires all line work to stay well inside the drawing area clear of the filing margins; numeral 124 is used both for the first channel's sensor and for "the connector current sensor 124 of each connector channel", so one numeral designates more than one part; and the Summary's recitation of the controller's couplings omits the connector current sensors that claim 1 requires. Prior-art characterizations in the Background were not traced to the inventor, per instruction. Note that no drawing pixels were inspected in this preflight.

findings.title: Connector-current sensing path asserted to be separate from, and not joined to, the isolated local bus
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md (sensing-line paragraph); draft/08-detailed-description.md (FIG. 1 paragraph describing what the bus carries; FIG. 3 paragraph listing the connections leaving the controller)
findings.detail: The coupling between the controller and the connector current sensors is inherent in the disclosed act of verification, so depicting a coupling line is a permissible convention. What is not traceable is the affirmative characterization of that coupling as a dedicated path that is distinct from, and expressly does not join, the isolated local bus. That is a connection/topology statement conveying technical substance (independence of the sensing channel from the control bus). No affirmative inventor passage describes how the connector current readings reach the controller. The nearest source passage is the bus sentence, which enumerates only the connector interfaces and contactors and says nothing about the sensors, and the verification sentence, which says only that the controller 'verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor'. The closed enumeration of the bus payload in the description reinforces the same unsupported exclusion.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-2.md): 'This line is the sensing connection by which the edge controller receives the connector current measured by the connector current sensor. It runs clear of the contactor outline, of the incoming vertical line and of the vehicle connector block, it neither touches nor joins the isolated local bus line, and it crosses no other line work.' Candidate (draft/08-detailed-description.md): 'The isolated local bus 108 carries, between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the pilot reports.' Nearest source (input/disclosure.md): 'A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus.' and 'The controller sends each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface and verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor.' No passage in the disclosure or the USER passage of the conversation states that the connector current sensors are read over a path separate from the isolated local bus, or that the bus does not carry the connector current measurements.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md, delete the exclusivity clause so the sentence reads: 'It runs clear of the contactor outline, of the incoming vertical line and of the vehicle connector block, and it crosses no other line work.' In draft/08-detailed-description.md, replace 'The isolated local bus 108 carries, between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the pilot reports.' with 'The isolated local bus 108 carries communications between the edge controller 106 and the connector channels, including the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the pilot reports.' Retain the plain coupling lines in FIG. 2 and FIG. 3 and the description sentence that the edge controller 106 is coupled to the connector current sensor of each connector channel, without characterizing that coupling as separate from the bus.

findings.title: FIG-2 brief contradicts its own margin constraint by ending a line at the drawing-area boundary
findings.detail: The brief instructs that all line work stay well inside the drawing area and clear of the filing margins, and then instructs the sensing line to continue upward and terminate at the upper boundary of the drawing area. The two instructions cannot both be satisfied, and a line terminating at the sheet boundary risks intruding into the filing margin. The remedy is to end the line short of the margin, which is how FIG. 1 handles the incoming supply ('Its left end reaches the left side of the dashed rectangle and stops there').
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-2.md): 'All line work stays well inside the drawing area, clear of the filing margins.' versus 'crosses the top side of the dashed rectangle, and continues upward to end at the upper boundary of the drawing area, as the connection that leads to the edge controller of FIG. 3.'
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md, replace 'and continues upward to end at the upper boundary of the drawing area, as the connection that leads to the edge controller of FIG. 3' with 'and continues upward to end at a free end well inside the upper part of the drawing area and clear of the filing margins, as the connection that leads to the edge controller of FIG. 3'.

findings.title: Numeral 124 used both for the first channel's sensor and for the sensor of every connector channel
findings.detail: Numeral 124 is introduced and defined in the FIG. 2 discussion as the connector current sensor of the first connector channel 120, and the numeral ledger lists it once as 'connector current sensor'. The FIG. 3 paragraph then attaches the same numeral to the sensor of every connector channel, so one numeral designates more than one part. Elsewhere the description correctly uses the unnumbered form 'the connector current sensor of that connector channel'.
findings.evidence: Candidate (draft/08-detailed-description.md, FIG. 2 paragraph): 'A connector current sensor 124 is arranged to measure a connector current delivered through the vehicle connector 128.' Candidate (draft/08-detailed-description.md, FIG. 3 paragraph): 'and to the connector current sensor 124 of each connector channel, shown in FIG. 2.'
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md, replace 'and to the connector current sensor 124 of each connector channel, shown in FIG. 2.' with 'and to the connector current sensor of each connector channel, such as the connector current sensor 124 shown in FIG. 2.'

findings.title: Summary omits the controller-to-connector-current-sensor coupling required by claim 1
findings.where: draft/06-summary.md (second paragraph, first sentence); draft/09-claims.md (claim 1, controller clause)
findings.detail: Claim 1 recites the controller as coupled to four things, including the connector current sensors. The Summary recites only three of them, so the summary of the invention states a narrower coupling relationship than the claim it summarizes. The Detailed Description does support the omitted coupling ('The edge controller 106 is coupled to the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel'), so this is a consistency repair only, and the coupling itself is traceable to the disclosed verification step.
findings.evidence: Candidate (draft/06-summary.md): 'A controller is coupled to the control-pilot interfaces, to the contactors and to the branch current sensor.' Candidate (draft/09-claims.md, claim 1): 'a controller coupled to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels, to the connector current sensors of the plurality of connector channels, to the contactors of the plurality of connector channels and to the branch current sensor'.
findings.fix: In draft/06-summary.md, replace 'A controller is coupled to the control-pilot interfaces, to the contactors and to the branch current sensor.' with 'A controller is coupled to the control-pilot interfaces, to the connector current sensors, to the contactors and to the branch current sensor.'
